title: Time-sync and hardware jitter tracing for KV eviction correlation
content:
Summary:
This note captures an investigative plan to diagnose recurring tail-latency spikes that align with KV-cache eviction bursts. Hypothesis: observable eviction bursts are amplified or misattributed due to host time synchronization drift and hardware-level clock-frequency jitter (GPU & CPU governors), making cross-host correlation noisy and reducing our ability to pinpoint root causes.

Goals:
- Define instrumentation & trace fields to reliably correlate eviction events with hardware-level signals across hosts.
- Produce compact dashboard widgets that surface time-offset problems and jitter fingerprints alongside eviction metrics.
- Provide an experimental runbook to distinguish true cache-origin latency events from artifacts caused by timestamp drift or clock-frequency changes.

Problem statement / context:
Operators have observed intermittent 95th/99th token-serving latency spikes that coincide with elevated kvcache_evictions. Existing dashboards show spikes but cross-host timelines look misaligned: some hosts show eviction events earlier/later than related downstream spans. We suspect two orthogonal contributors: (1) clock synchronization errors between hosts (NTP jitter, transient offset) and (2) hardware-induced timestamp variability (e.g., GPU frequency scaling changes causing nvml timestamp samples to shift relative to monotonic time). Both make trace alignment and automated correlation (span join by timestamp window) unreliable.

Principles for instrumentation:
- Always emit both wall-clock and monotonic timestamps in critical spans: e.g., span.start_wall_ns, span.start_monotonic_ns, span.end_monotonic_ns. Monotonic timestamps are primary for ordering; wall-clock is for human-friendly labels and cross-dataset joins when offsets are known.
- Add a compact host offset heartbeat on every trace: host_clock_offset_ns (monotonic -> wall delta measured at trace creation).
- Capture lightweight hardware telemetry snapshots in key spans (as optional low-cardinality tags): nvml_gpu_clock_mhz, cpu_scaling_governor, cpu_max_freq_khz, host_ntp_age_ms (time since last NTP correction), host_ptp_status.
- Expose kvcache-specific counters in trace context: kvcache_hits, kvcache_evicted_count, kvcache_prefetch_hits, kvcache_eviction_reason (e.g., ttl, memory-pressure, lrucull). Keep values compact and numeric.

Span design suggestions (fields & semantic anchors):
- span.name: "kvcache:eviction-batch" (emit when eviction happens), fields: {evicted_count, bin_id, eviction_reason, host_monotonic_ns, host_wall_ns, host_clock_offset_ns}.
- span.name: "gpu:freq-change" (emit on GPU freq change event observed locally), fields: {old_mhz, new_mhz, nvml_time_monotonic_ns, host_monotonic_ns}.
- span.name: "request:serve" (primary token-serving span) augmented with {kvcache_warmth_index, session_id, host_monotonic_ns}.
- Trace-level tags: primary_host, replica_set_id, model_variant, rollout_tag.

Correlation strategy (how traces map to dashboards):
- Use monotonic timestamps as the canonical alignment axis. Convert distributed event timestamps to a monotonic reference using the provided host_clock_offset_ns per-trace.
- For cross-host aggregation, compute per-host offset distributions (wall_monotonic_offset = wall - monotonic) over N-minute windows and display median and 99th offset to detect skew.
- When joining eviction events to request traces, prefer join window based on monotonic delta (e.g., +-250ms) and only fall back to wall-clock join when hosts report stable offset (median offset variance < 5ms).

Metric definitions (compact):
- kvcache_eviction_rate_per_min: number of evictions per-minute per-host.
- kvcache_tail_latency_ms: 95/99 percentile token-latency for requests that see eviction within join window.
- host_monotonic_offset_ms_distribution: histogram of (wall - monotonic)/1e6 per-host.
- gpu_clock_switch_rate_per_min: rate of frequency-change spans emitted.
- host_ntp_correction_events: count of NTP corrections > 10ms in last 10m.

Dashboard widgets (prioritized):
1) Eviction + Monotonic-aligned Waterfall: a small waterfall that lays out request:serve spans and overlays kvcache:eviction-batch spans aligned on _monotonic_ time. Color requests by whether they saw eviction within window. Allows quick visual confirmation of causality.
2) Host Offset Distribution (line + bands): per-host median and 99th wall-monotonic offset over last 24h. Annotate manual NTP/PTP syncs.
3) Eviction Heatmap by Host + GPU Clock: 2D heatmap where X=time, Y=host, cell intensity is eviction rate; overlay small markers when gpu_clock_switch_rate spikes.
4) Tail-latency attribution panel: group requests by (eviction in window vs no-eviction) and show p95/p99 token-latency with counts and KV-cache warmth index distribution.
5) Hardware Jitter Events timeline: compact list of gpu:freq-change events, host_ntp_correction_events, and kernel OOM notifications (if any), with quick links to traces.

Experiment / runbook (step-by-step):
1) Safe logging rollout: add monotonic + host_clock_offset fields to request:serve traces on a 10% traffic sampling for 24–48h.
2) Collect baseline: compute per-host offset histograms and gpu_clock_switch_rate for two days. Look for hosts with >10ms median offset or >50ms 99th.
3) Narrow join window: re-run offline joins using monotonic alignment and compare correlation score (fraction of eviction-correlated high-latency traces) vs previous wall-clock joins.
4) Induce controlled GPU frequency change test on a single host (low traffic lane): toggle governor and observe whether eviction join stability changes or the perceived timing of eviction batches shifts.
5) If offsets exceed threshold, schedule targeted NTP/PTP fix and re-evaluate.

Data retention & cost notes:
- Emit hardware telemetry as low-cardinality numeric fields to avoid high cardinality costs.
- Sample traces for full field emission; for every 1 in 10 traces emit full hardware snapshot, otherwise limited set.

Ownership & next steps:
- Owner: Aisha Patel (eng-observability) - drive the instrumentation PR and dashboard prototype.
- Engineering collaborator: Marcus Chen - implement monotonic timestamp plumbing in serving runtime.
- SRE collaborator: Lena Ortiz - run controlled tests on staging fleet and manage host sync upgrades.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Do all our runtime languages expose a reliable monotonic timer with nanosecond precision across environments? (Action: runtime team to verify.)
- Should we default to PTP for production fleet time sync in regions with persistent drift? (Cost/ops tradeoff.)
- How to expose nvml snapshots in air-gapped Private deployments where NVML access may be restricted? Fallback: expose a boolean flag gpu_freq_flap_detected and approximate rates.

Appendix: quick example trace snippet (conceptual)
- trace.tags: {primary_host: "host-123", host_clock_offset_ns: 4200000} 
- span request:serve: {start_monotonic_ns: 239402394023, start_wall_ns: 239406624023, kvcache_warmth_index: 0.22} 
- span kvcache:eviction-batch: {evicted_count: 84, host_monotonic_ns: 239402394170} 

This doc is a working plan — aim to get instrumentation merged behind a feature-flag for canary testing within two sprints. After the first data collection window, we will reconvene and decide whether to (a) iterate instrumentation, (b) schedule fleet sync fixes, or (c) attribute root cause to genuine workload behavior (prefetch misconfiguration, model fanout).

Notes to self: track JIRA-OBS-312, coordinate with runtime PR #987, schedule 30m sync with SRE and GPU infra owners post-canary.
